title: OutpostRefusal
description: Why an outpost did not execute a call it received: the body of the door's `refuse` verb. A code from a closed list and nothing else (ADR 0148 §9): it names a class of refusal and never the rule that produced it (ADR 0147 §10). Whatever the code, the endpoint's server did not receive the call.

code.description: `unknown_endpoint`: the policy file has no endpoint under this alias. `tool_not_allowed`: the tool is outside the endpoint's patterns. `write_denied`: the endpoint denies writes and its server does not declare the tool read-only. `payload_too_large`: the arguments weigh more than the endpoint's ceiling. `busy`: the concurrency ceiling is reached, or the outpost is stopping. `endpoint_unavailable`: the outpost could not reach or open its own server, and sent it nothing. `unsupported_kind`: the daemon does not know this kind of call. `signature_refused`: the call is not signed by a key the outpost's policy file pins, or its signature binds another call, another instance or another envelope; the envelope was not opened. `call_unreadable`: the envelope does not open with this instance's key, or what it holds is not a call. `deadline_passed`: the deadline had passed before the outpost could start. `cancelled`: the door cancelled the call before the outpost started it.
